posts.title: Token Costs Are Becoming The New EDA Budget Battle
posts.summary:
Cost per token is causing EDA design budgets to balloon; what comes next isn't entirely clear yet.
The post Token Costs Are Becoming The New EDA Budget Battle appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The adoption of agentic AI in chip design is introducing a new variable into EDA budgets: the recurring cost per token for AI-assisted design and verification.
Design teams are now prioritizing 'token efficiency' to ensure that the ROI of AI tools justifies the operational expense of running large language models.
Industry experts warn that while AI offers design acceleration, the high cost of potential errors in chip manufacturing makes verification and trust in AI outputs more critical than ever.

posts.title: When Digital Forensics Reaches The Hardware Layer
posts.summary:
Security controls are increasingly implemented in ways that can limit access to information required for an investigation.
The post When Digital Forensics Reaches The Hardware Layer appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Modern hardware-based security features like Secure Boot, TEEs, and encrypted storage are increasingly blocking traditional software-level forensic data extraction.
Forensic investigators are now forced to pivot toward hardware security testing to bypass physical protections that restrict access to stored data.
Successful investigations now require deep expertise in hardware architecture, schematics, and silicon-level security implementations rather than just software analysis.

posts.title: Batteries just broke another record in the US
posts.summary: Battery installations hit a new record in the US in the second quarter of 2026. In total, 20.2 gigawatt-hours of new capacity came online, according to a new report. That’s enough to supply the daily electricity needs of about 700,000 homes. The surge is putting the country on a trajectory to see 71 gigawatt-hours of…
bullets: US battery storage capacity hit a record 20.2 gigawatt-hours in Q2 2026, with projections suggesting a 20% annual increase to 71 gigawatt-hours for the full year.
Utility-scale projects are driving the market surge, while residential battery installations are expected to decline by 16% in 2026 following the expiration of key tax credits in 2025.
Data centers are currently the primary growth driver in the behind-the-meter commercial sector, accounting for approximately 75% of new installations.
Industry analysts highlight a strategic shift toward domestic US-made battery technology as the market matures and demand for grid stability increases.

The concentration of advanced AI research within a few frontier companies raises concerns about the future role of human mathematicians and the erosion of traditional academic collaboration norms.
Entrepreneur Danijar Hafner is shifting his focus from virtual world models to physical robotics, aiming to enable AI agents to navigate real-world environments.

posts.title: OpenAI Does Math, Reward-Hacking, Meta Launches Personal Agent
posts.summary: OpenAI solving one of the most famous math problems is extremely impressive, and of little impact to most people's lives; Meta's Muse agent launch has the potential to be the exact opposite.
bullets: OpenAI has achieved a significant technical milestone by solving a complex, high-level math problem, demonstrating advanced reasoning capabilities.
Despite the technical impressiveness of OpenAI's math breakthrough, its immediate practical utility for the average user remains limited.
Meta’s launch of the 'Muse' personal agent represents a shift toward consumer-facing AI applications with high potential for broad, daily impact.
The contrast between these two developments highlights the industry divide between pure research breakthroughs and the deployment of functional, user-centric AI tools.
